title: UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028: Expression of Interest for Artists, Creative Businesses, Organisations and Cultural Institutions
summary: The UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 is creating a major platform for artists, creative businesses, cultural organisations and institutions across the United Kingdom and Nigeria to develop new partnerships, exchange ideas and showcase creative work to international audiences. Delivered by the British Council in partnership with Nigeria’s Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy , the Season will run from June to December 2028 , with legacy activity continuing into 2029. The programme is designed to strengthen the long-term creative relationship between the UK and Nigeria by creating connections between people, organisations and creative industries in both countries. The initiative is particularly significant because it comes a decade after the landmark 2015/16 UK–Nigeria Season, at a time when Nigeria’s creative economy has expanded considerably and the UK and Nigeria are seeking deeper cultural, commercial and institutional connections. UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028: What Is It About? The UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 is a bilateral cultural initiative bringing together creative communities from both countries. The Season aims to celebrate the creativity, diversity and cultural heritage of the UK and Nigeria while creating opportunities for collaboration that can continue long after the 2028 programme ends. According to the British Council, the Season is intended to: Strengthen the creative partnership between the UK and Nigeria. Build lasting professional and institutional connections. Create opportunities for creative collaboration. Open pathways to new markets and audiences. Showcase the depth and diversity of UK and Nigerian creative talent. Support knowledge exchange between creative professionals and institutions. Encourage new artistic commissions and collaborative projects. Strengthen creative infrastructure and systems. Support longer-term relationships that can continue beyond the Season itself. The wider bilateral initiative is also expected to contribute to skills development, institutional capacity, market access and international connections across the creative economy. When Will the UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 Take Place? The main Season will take place from: June to December 2028 Legacy activities are expected to continue into 2029 , meaning that the programme is intended to have an impact beyond the main 2028 calendar. However, creative professionals and organisations do not have to wait until 2028 to become involved. The programme is already seeking ideas, partnerships and potential collaborations during the preparation and incubation period. The British Council has described the period before the Season as an opportunity for partner engagement, visiting delegations and programme incubation, helping potential collaborations develop before activities take place in 2028. Five Key Focus Areas of the Season The UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 is organised around five major focus areas. Applicants and potential partners should consider how their proposed idea connects with one or more of these areas. 1. Cultural Heritage, Identity and Infrastructure This focus area recognises the importance of cultural heritage and identity while considering the infrastructure required for the creative sector to thrive. Projects could explore cultural heritage, storytelling, identity, preservation, cultural spaces, creative infrastructure and related issues. The emphasis is not simply on presenting culture, but also on strengthening the systems and structures that enable cultural and creative activity to develop sustainably. 2. Market Access and Mutual Growth The Season also aims to create stronger connections between creative industries and markets in both countries. This focus area is relevant to organisations, entrepreneurs and creative professionals seeking opportunities to: Reach new audiences. Build international networks. Develop commercial partnerships. Expand into new markets. Connect with buyers, investors or industry professionals. Strengthen the international visibility of their creative work or business. The broader UK–Nigeria creative partnership has also identified international market access and structured engagement as important areas for strengthening the creative economy. 3. Creative Collaboration and Partnerships Partnership is at the heart of the Season. The programme is interested in ideas that bring together people, organisations and institutions from the UK and Nigeria to develop meaningful creative collaborations. A proposed project does not necessarily need to be completely developed before an expression of interest is submitted. The opportunity specifically welcomes both developed project concepts and early-stage ideas. If you already have a potential partner in the other country, you can indicate this in your response. If you do not yet have a partner, you can still express your interest and describe the type of collaboration you would like to develop. 4. New Artistic Commissions The Season will also provide a platform for new creative and artistic work. This could create possibilities for artists and creative organisations to propose original projects, productions, performances, commissions or other forms of creative activity that contribute to the UK–Nigeria cultural relationship. The emphasis is on developing ideas capable of creating meaningful artistic and cultural value for audiences in both countries. 5. Research, Policy and Knowledge Exchange The Season is not limited to performances and exhibitions. Research, policy discussions, professional learning and knowledge exchange are also part of its vision. This focus area can be particularly relevant to institutions, researchers, cultural policy professionals, academics, practitioners and organisations working on issues affecting the creative and cultural sectors. It recognises that long-term creative development requires not only artistic activity but also research, evidence, policy development, institutional learning and the exchange of knowledge between countries. Which Artforms and Creative Disciplines Are Eligible? One of the notable features of the UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 is its broad approach to creative disciplines. The Season is open to all artforms and creative disciplines , rather than restricting participation to a single artistic field. Potential areas include: Music Film Visual arts Fashion Literature Digital creativity Performing arts Theatre Dance Architecture Gaming Gastronomy Craft Creative technology Other creative and cultural disciplines This broad scope means that the opportunity may be relevant to both traditional and emerging areas of the creative economy. The British Council s wider arts work in Nigeria similarly spans areas including architecture, design, fashion, film, literature, music, theatre, dance and visual arts. Who Is Being Invited to Get Involved? The opportunity is aimed at people and organisations within the cultural and creative sectors of both the UK and Nigeria . The invitation specifically mentions: Artists Creative businesses Cultural organisations Cultural institutions Creative-sector organisations Other relevant institutions and creative practitioners The British Council is looking for people and organisations with an idea for a project, partnership or collaboration that could contribute to the UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028. You do not necessarily need to have a fully developed project. The programme welcomes: Fully formed project proposals. Early-stage creative ideas. Potential partnerships. Collaboration concepts. Ideas that could be developed with a partner in the other country. This makes the expression of interest particularly useful for creative professionals who have a strong concept but may still be exploring how to develop it internationally. Important: This Is Not a Funding Application One of the most important points for anyone considering submitting an expression of interest is that this stage is not a funding application . The purpose of the current Expression of Interest is to: Gather creative ideas. Identify potential partners. Understand what the creative sectors in the UK and Nigeria would like to develop. Start conversations between potential collaborators. Explore projects that could form part of the wider Season. Help shape future programme development. Therefore, applicants should not approach the EOI as though they are applying for a conventional grant. Instead, the focus should be on clearly communicating who you are, what you would like to do, how your idea connects to the Season and whether you already have a partner in the other country . What Should You Include in Your Expression of Interest? The response should be no more than two pages . It should cover four essential areas: 1. Who You Are Introduce yourself, your organisation, institution, creative business or relevant professional background. Explain your role within the cultural or creative sector and provide enough information for the organisers to understand your experience and relevance to the proposed idea. 2. What You Would Like to Do Describe your project, partnership or collaboration idea. This does not have to be a fully developed proposal. If the concept is still at an early stage, explain the idea clearly and describe what you hope to develop. 3. Which Focus Area Your Idea Fits Explain which of the Season s five focus areas your idea relates to: Cultural heritage, identity and infrastructure Market access and mutual growth Creative collaboration and partnerships New artistic commissions Research, policy and knowledge exchange If your project connects with more than one focus area, you can explain those connections. 4. Whether You Have a Partner in the Other Country State whether you already have a UK or Nigerian partner. For example, a Nigerian creative organisation could identify a UK institution it already works with, while a UK artist could describe an existing relationship with a Nigerian creative organisation. If you do not yet have a partner, explain the type of partner or collaboration you would like to develop. How to Submit Your Expression of Interest The Expression of Interest should be submitted by email to: UKNigeria.SeasonofCulture@britishcouncil.org The response should be two pages or fewer and should address the requested information. The stated deadline is: 14 September 2026 This deadline is important for anyone intending to have their idea considered as part of the current expression-of-interest process. For official information and updates, visit the https://www.britishcouncil.org.ng/programmes/arts/uk-nigeria-season-culture-2028 Online Information Sessions for Interested Applicants Two online sessions are being held to help potential participants understand the Expression of Interest process, the Season and what is expected in a response. Session 1 Date: Monday, 17 August 2026 Time: 11:00 WAT Session 2 Date: Monday, 7 September 2026 Time: 11:00 WAT Both sessions cover the same information, so participants can attend one or both. If you have questions before attending the sessions, you can contact the Season team by email at: UKNigeria.SeasonofCulture@britishcouncil.org Why Should Creative Professionals Consider Getting Involved? The UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 presents an opportunity to engage with a major bilateral cultural initiative at an early stage. For creative professionals and organisations, early involvement can be particularly valuable because the current process is designed to identify ideas and potential partners before the main Season takes place. Potential areas of value include: Developing UK–Nigeria creative partnerships. Building international professional networks. Exploring new audiences and markets. Developing collaborative creative projects. Connecting creative institutions across both countries. Contributing ideas to a major international cultural programme. Exploring new artistic commissions. Sharing knowledge and expertise. Strengthening international visibility. Building relationships that may continue beyond 2028. The broader bilateral programme is intended to establish lasting partnerships rather than relationships that end when the Season closes. The British Council has highlighted institutional partnerships, skills development, market access and sustainable creative connections as important elements of the wider initiative. A Major Opportunity for the UK and Nigerian Creative Economies The Season arrives at an important period for creative industries in both countries. Nigeria has developed one of Africa s most internationally visible creative economies, while the UK has a well-established global creative sector spanning music, film, fashion, theatre, literature, design, gaming and other industries. The Season provides a structured platform for these ecosystems to connect. Rather than treating cultural exchange simply as a series of performances or exhibitions, the initiative takes a broader approach that includes creative enterprise, partnerships, infrastructure, policy, research, skills and international market access. The British Council has also described the 2028 Season as part of a wider effort to strengthen creative systems and production infrastructure, develop skills and leadership, improve access to international markets and create lasting relationships between UK and Nigerian creative institutions. What Happened During the Previous UK–Nigeria Season? The 2028 programme builds on the earlier UK–Nigeria Season, which ran from September 2015 to March 2017 . The previous Season demonstrated the potential scale of UK–Nigeria cultural collaboration. According to the British Council, the 2015/16 Season: Covered nine artforms. Delivered 31 projects. Involved 79 partner organisations. Reached 12 cities. Attracted more than 446,000 attendees to live events. Trained 7,135 artists. The new Season therefore represents a return to a successful model of cultural exchange, while responding to the significant growth and transformation of the creative sector over the intervening decade. What Makes the 2028 Season Different? The creative environment in which the 2028 Season is being developed is significantly different from that of the previous Season. Digital technology, international streaming, gaming, creative entrepreneurship, social media, emerging technologies and rapidly changing global markets have transformed how artists and creative businesses reach audiences. The 2028 Season is therefore positioned not only as a celebration of culture but also as a platform for developing stronger creative systems and international relationships. The British Council has identified areas such as emerging technology, creative infrastructure, professional skills, leadership, international markets and institutional partnerships as part of the wider UK–Nigeria creative collaboration agenda. Tips for Preparing a Strong Expression of Interest Although the EOI is limited to two pages, applicants should make every sentence count. Keep the idea clear Avoid filling the document with unnecessary background information. Clearly explain what you want to do and why it matters. Explain the UK–Nigeria connection Since this is a bilateral Season, make the connection between the two countries clear. Explain how the project could create meaningful collaboration between Nigerian and UK creative communities, institutions, businesses or audiences. Connect the idea to a focus area Do not simply name one of the five focus areas. Explain why your idea belongs there. Be realistic If your project is still at an early stage, say so. The EOI specifically welcomes early ideas, so there is no need to present an undeveloped concept as though it is already fully formed. Highlight your experience Briefly demonstrate why you or your organisation are well positioned to develop the idea. Relevant previous projects, partnerships, creative work, audiences or institutional experience can help provide context. Explain your partnership status Clearly state whether you already have a partner in the UK or Nigeria. If you do not, explain what type of partner you would like to work with. Stay within the two-page limit The request is for a response of two pages or fewer , so concise and structured communication is important. Who Can Apply or Express Interest? The opportunity is intended for the cultural and creative sectors in the United Kingdom and Nigeria . Potential participants include: Individual artists. Creative businesses. Cultural organisations. Cultural institutions. Creative-sector organisations. Other relevant organisations or practitioners with suitable project or collaboration ideas. There is no specific race or ethnicity requirement stated in the information provided for this Expression of Interest. The opportunity is geographically centred on the UK and Nigeria , rather than being presented as a general worldwide opportunity for applicants from every country. Importantly, eligibility is described in terms of participation in the UK or Nigerian cultural and creative sectors. Therefore, prospective participants should focus on demonstrating their connection to the relevant creative sector and explaining how their proposed idea contributes to UK–Nigeria collaboration. Is This a Grant or Scholarship? No. The current Expression of Interest is explicitly not a funding application . It is a process for gathering ideas, identifying partners and initiating conversations about potential projects for the Season. Participants should therefore not assume that submitting an EOI automatically provides funding, a grant, a scholarship, employment or another financial award. Any future project development or support arrangements would depend on subsequent discussions and the programme s development. Key Details at a Glance Opportunity: UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 – Expression of Interest Main Season: June–December 2028 Legacy activity: Through 2029 Countries: United Kingdom and Nigeria Creative disciplines: All artforms and creative disciplines Who can express interest: Artists, organisations, institutions and creative businesses in the UK and Nigeria Maximum response length: Two pages Submission method: Email Submission email: UKNigeria.SeasonofCulture@britishcouncil.org Deadline: 14 September 2026 Application type: Expression of Interest, not a funding application Organisers: British Council and Nigeria s Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy How to Find More Information Those interested in participating should consult the official British Council information and follow any updates to the Expression of Interest process. https://www.britishcouncil.org.ng/uknigeria-2015-16-impact-report More opportunities here, https://opportunitiesforyouth.org The post UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028: Expression of Interest for Artists, Creative Businesses, Organisations and Cultural Institutions appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program at Bank of America: Apply in São Paulo
summary: The 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program offers university students an opportunity to gain practical experience in investment banking with Bank of America in São Paulo, Brazil. The internship is designed for students pursuing disciplines such as Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, or related fields who want to build experience in corporate finance, mergers and acquisitions, debt and equity financing, financial analysis, and client advisory. The position is listed as an Off-cycle Internship under Job ID JR-14454 and is based in São Paulo, Brazil . According to the official Bank of America careers listing, applications are open until December 31, 2027 . For students interested in pursuing careers in investment banking, corporate finance, financial advisory, capital markets, or related areas, this opportunity can provide exposure to the type of transactions and financial solutions that support companies and contribute to the broader global economy. Opportunity Overview Opportunity: 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program Position: Investment Banking Intern Organization: Bank of America Location: São Paulo, Brazil Job ID: JR-14454 Internship type: Off-cycle internship Work arrangement: In-person or hybrid Working hours: 30 hours per week Minimum age: 18 years Application deadline: December 31, 2027 Required language: Fluent English Eligible academic backgrounds: Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, and related courses The official listing confirms that the role is intended for students who are currently studying, attend classes in the morning, and expect to graduate in one year or more. About the Bank of America Brazil Investment Banking Group Investment banking is an area of financial services focused on helping companies, institutions, and other organizations make significant financial and strategic decisions. The Brazil Investment Banking group at Bank of America provides advisory expertise across major corporate finance activities. According to the vacancy announcement, the team works around Mergers and Acquisitions (M A), Debt underwriting, and Equity underwriting , providing integrated financial solutions to clients. This means an intern joining the team may be exposed to an environment where financial analysis, corporate strategy, market knowledge, communication, and client service come together. Mergers and Acquisitions Mergers and acquisitions involve transactions in which companies combine, acquire other businesses, sell businesses, or restructure ownership. Investment banking professionals supporting M A transactions may be involved in activities such as: Financial analysis Company and industry research Valuation Preparation of financial models Analysis of potential transactions Preparation of presentations and transaction materials Supporting due diligence processes Monitoring market developments Preparing information for clients and senior bankers For an intern, exposure to M A can provide valuable insight into how major corporate transactions are evaluated and executed. Debt Underwriting Debt underwriting involves helping companies and institutions raise capital through debt markets. Investment banking teams may help clients evaluate financing requirements, structure transactions, assess market conditions, and connect borrowers with investors. Students interested in corporate finance can therefore gain a better understanding of how businesses finance expansion, acquisitions, operations, and other strategic objectives. Equity Underwriting Equity underwriting involves helping companies raise capital through the issuance of shares or other equity-related securities. This area requires an understanding of financial markets, company performance, valuation, investor considerations, and broader economic conditions. Exposure to equity transactions can help students understand how businesses access capital markets and how investors evaluate investment opportunities. Who Is Bank of America Looking For? The internship is targeted at university students with relevant academic backgrounds and an interest in investment banking. According to the official vacancy, applicants should meet several important requirements. 1. Students in Relevant Academic Disciplines Applicants should be studying: Business Economics Accounting Engineering Related courses This broad academic requirement means that the opportunity is not restricted exclusively to traditional finance or economics students. Students from other related disciplines may also be considered if their academic background and skills are relevant to investment banking. Engineering students, for example, may bring quantitative, analytical, problem-solving, and technical skills that can be valuable in financial analysis. 2. Morning Shift Students The vacancy specifically states that applicants should be morning shift students . This requirement is important because candidates should assess their university timetable before applying. The internship requires availability for 30 hours per week, so applicants need to determine whether their academic schedule can accommodate the required working hours. 3. Students With at Least One Year Remaining Before Graduation Applicants are expected to graduate in one year or more . This is an important eligibility condition. Students who are very close to graduation should carefully evaluate whether they satisfy the requirement before submitting an application. The program is particularly relevant to students who still have sufficient time remaining in their degree to undertake an internship while continuing their studies. 4. Fluent English Fluent English is mandatory for the position. Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating in English in a professional environment. Strong English communication can be particularly important in investment banking because professionals may need to: Communicate with colleagues Prepare written materials Participate in meetings Understand financial documentation Present analysis Communicate with clients and stakeholders Work in an international business environment Applicants whose English is not yet at a professional level should consider strengthening their written and spoken communication skills before applying. 5. Availability for 30 Hours Per Week Candidates must be available to work 30 hours per week . The internship can be undertaken in an in-person or hybrid format , according to the vacancy information. Applicants should therefore be prepared to commit substantial weekly time to the internship while continuing their studies. Key Skills Required for the Investment Banking Internship Beyond academic qualifications, Bank of America identifies several skills that are relevant to the position. Strong Knowledge of Corporate Finance A strong understanding of corporate finance is one of the most important foundations for an investment banking career. Applicants should ideally understand concepts such as: Financial statements Cash flow Capital structure Cost of capital Valuation Debt financing Equity financing Corporate investment decisions Profitability Financial performance Risk and return Students who can demonstrate practical understanding rather than simply memorizing definitions may be better prepared for the demands of the role. Macroeconomic Knowledge The vacancy also highlights macroeconomic knowledge . Investment banking decisions do not happen in isolation. Economic conditions can influence companies, investors, capital markets, financing costs, mergers, acquisitions, and investment decisions. Applicants should therefore develop an understanding of issues such as: Economic growth Inflation Interest rates Monetary policy Fiscal policy Exchange rates Employment Global economic trends Financial market conditions Keeping up with major economic developments can also help candidates demonstrate genuine interest in financial markets during recruitment. Strong Communication Skills Investment banking requires more than numerical ability. Professionals must communicate complex financial information clearly to colleagues, clients, executives, investors, and other stakeholders. Strong communication skills can include: Clear writing Professional speaking Presentation skills Active listening Ability to explain complex concepts Attention to detail Professional correspondence Team communication For students from communication, business, economics, accounting, engineering, and other disciplines, developing the ability to translate technical information into clear business language can be particularly valuable. Client Focus The position also emphasizes client focus . Investment banking is fundamentally a client-oriented business. Bankers work with organizations facing significant strategic, financial, and corporate decisions. Candidates should therefore demonstrate an understanding of: Professionalism Client service Confidentiality Responsiveness Attention to client requirements Problem-solving Business judgment Teamwork A candidate who can demonstrate that they understand the importance of delivering high-quality work for clients can strengthen their overall profile. What Students Can Gain From an Investment Banking Internship An investment banking internship can be valuable for students who want to understand how the financial sector operates in practice. Although the exact responsibilities assigned to an intern will depend on the team and business needs, working within an investment banking environment can provide exposure to areas such as financial analysis, corporate transactions, market research, client service, and professional financial communication. Potential areas of professional development include: Practical Corporate Finance Exposure Students can move beyond classroom theory and gain an understanding of how financial concepts are applied in real business situations. Understanding of Major Corporate Transactions The Brazil Investment Banking group works across M A, debt, and equity activities, giving the role a strong connection to major corporate finance transactions. Professional Workplace Experience The internship provides an opportunity to work within a major global financial institution and experience professional expectations around communication, teamwork, deadlines, accuracy, and client service. Financial Market Knowledge Students can strengthen their understanding of how economic and market conditions affect companies and financial transactions. Career Development Experience in investment banking can be relevant to future careers in: Investment banking Corporate finance Private equity Asset management Financial advisory Corporate strategy Capital markets Consulting Commercial banking Financial analysis The experience can therefore be useful for students considering a long-term career in finance or related business fields. Why São Paulo Is an Important Location for This Opportunity São Paulo is one of Brazil s most important financial and business centers. For students pursuing financial careers, an internship in São Paulo can provide exposure to Brazil s corporate and financial environment while allowing participants to work within an international financial institution. The location is particularly relevant to applicants interested in emerging markets, Latin American finance, multinational corporations, and cross-border business. Applicants who are not currently based in São Paulo should pay close attention to the position s in-person or hybrid requirements and determine whether they can realistically meet the workplace expectations. Age Requirement The vacancy specifies that applicants must be at least 18 years old . Candidates who are below 18 should therefore not assume that they qualify simply because they meet the academic requirements. Work Arrangement The internship offers an in-person or hybrid format , with a commitment of 30 hours per week . The flexibility of a hybrid arrangement may be useful for some students, but applicants should not interpret hybrid as meaning that the internship is fully remote. Candidates should be prepared to participate in the working arrangement required by the employer. Application Deadline The stated application deadline for the 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program is: December 31, 2027 Applicants are encouraged not to wait until the final day to submit their applications. Recruitment processes can involve multiple stages, and preparing a strong application in advance gives candidates more time to review their information and ensure that all required materials are complete. The official Bank of America careers page currently lists December 31, 2027 as the application deadline. How to Apply Interested applicants should apply through the official Bank of America careers platform. When applying, candidates should carefully review the official vacancy requirements and provide accurate academic, professional, and personal information. Applicants should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates: Their current academic program. Their expected graduation date. Their relevant academic knowledge. Their interest in investment banking. Their understanding of corporate finance. Their communication abilities. Their analytical and problem-solving skills. Their availability to work 30 hours per week. Their English proficiency. Their suitability for an in-person or hybrid position in São Paulo. APPLY HERE How to Make Your Application Stronger Meeting the minimum requirements is only one part of a competitive application. Candidates should also make an effort to demonstrate why they are genuinely interested in investment banking. Tailor Your Resume Avoid submitting a generic resume that does not highlight finance-related capabilities. Where applicable, emphasize: Financial analysis Economics Accounting Corporate finance Research Data analysis Business projects Leadership Teamwork Presentations Communication Problem-solving Relevant internships Extracurricular activities Highlight Relevant Coursework Students should consider highlighting courses relevant to investment banking, including: Corporate Finance Financial Accounting Economics Statistics Business Mathematics Investment Analysis Financial Markets Business Strategy Valuation Demonstrate Analytical Ability Investment banking is highly analytical, so applicants should identify experiences where they have analyzed information, solved complex problems, interpreted data, or made evidence-based recommendations. This does not necessarily have to come from previous employment. Academic projects, case competitions, student organizations, research projects, and other activities can also demonstrate analytical ability. Demonstrate Communication Skills Because communication is specifically identified as an important skill for the role, candidates should make sure their application reflects strong written communication. A resume that is clear, logically organized, concise, and free from avoidable errors can help demonstrate professionalism. Research Bank of America and Investment Banking Candidates should understand the organization and the business area they are applying to. Before an interview or assessment, applicants should research: Bank of America s business operations Investment banking M A Debt markets Equity markets Current economic conditions Brazil s financial environment Major trends affecting corporate finance This preparation can help candidates provide stronger and more informed responses during recruitment. Visit HERE to learn more about the Frequently Asked Questions What is the 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program? It is an off-cycle Investment Banking Intern position with Bank of America in São Paulo, Brazil, designed for students pursuing Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, or related courses. Where is the internship located? The position is based in São Paulo, Brazil . Is the internship remote? No. The official listing specifies an in-person or hybrid internship format. How many hours per week does the internship require? Applicants must be available to work 30 hours per week . What degree programs are eligible? The vacancy identifies Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, and related courses as relevant academic backgrounds. Do I need to speak English? Yes. Fluent English is mandatory according to the official job posting. What age do I need to be? Applicants must be at least 18 years old . When is the application deadline? The stated deadline is December 31, 2027 . What job ID should applicants look for? The position is listed under JR-14454 . Is this a graduate job? No. It is an internship opportunity for current students . Applicants are expected to have one year or more remaining before graduation. Important Note for International Applicants The information provided in the official vacancy confirms the academic, language, age, schedule, and work-format requirements, but applicants from outside Brazil should carefully review the official application and employment requirements before applying. International candidates should not automatically assume that being academically eligible means they are authorized to undertake an internship in Brazil. Any applicable immigration, work authorization, residency, or local employment requirements should be independently confirmed through the appropriate official channels. The official vacancy should remain the primary source for the most current application requirements. Conclusion The 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program at Bank of America is a valuable opportunity for students who want to begin building a career in investment banking and corporate finance. Based in São Paulo, the internship offers exposure to a financial environment focused on major activities including Mergers and Acquisitions, debt underwriting, and equity underwriting . The opportunity is particularly suited to students studying Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, or related disciplines who have a strong interest in corporate finance and financial markets. Candidates must be at least 18 years old, fluent in English, attend classes in the morning, expect to graduate in one year or more, and be available to work 30 hours per week in an in-person or hybrid format. With the application deadline set for December 31, 2027 , interested students have an opportunity to prepare their resumes, strengthen their corporate finance and macroeconomic knowledge, research the investment banking industry, and submit a carefully tailored application. Students who are serious about entering investment banking should view this type of internship not simply as a temporary placement, but as an opportunity to develop technical knowledge, professional communication skills, financial-market awareness, and practical experience that can support future careers across finance and business. title: ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 in Belgium: Fully Funded Study and Professional Training Opportunities for Applicants from 32 Eligible Countries
summary: The ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 offer an opportunity for qualified graduates and working professionals from selected developing and partner countries to undertake specialised higher education and professional training in Belgium. The programme is administered by the Académie de Recherche et d’Enseignement Supérieur (ARES) and supports specialised academic and professional programmes within the higher education system of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation in Belgium. For the 2027–2028 call, applicants can choose from one specialised bachelor s programme, eight specialised master s programmes, and one continuing education programme . Applications opened on 3 August 2026 , and the application deadline is Friday, 18 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Belgian time (UTC+1) . Applicants are strongly advised to begin the process early because the application requires account creation, documentation, eligibility checks and submission through the ARES GIRAF platform. ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 at a Glance Host country: Belgium Organiser: Académie de Recherche et d’Enseignement Supérieur (ARES) Academic year: 2027–2028 Application opening date: 3 August 2026 Application deadline: 18 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Belgian time (UTC+1) Study location: Institutions within the Wallonia-Brussels Federation Available programmes: 1 specialised bachelor s degree, 8 specialised master s degrees and 1 continuing education programme Duration: Up to 12 months for the specialised bachelor s and master s programmes; up to 6 months for continuing education Eligible applicants: Residents and workers from 32 eligible partner countries, with a special provision for Palestinian nationals Application platform: ARES GIRAF Application limit: One programme per applicant Funding: International travel, living/subsistence support, applicable tuition fees, insurance and certain visa-related or other eligible costs What Are the ARES International Training Scholarships? The ARES International Training Scholarships are designed to strengthen the academic knowledge, technical expertise and professional capacity of people from eligible partner countries. Rather than being a general scholarship open to applicants from every country, the programme targets candidates from a defined group of partner countries. Applicants are expected to demonstrate both academic preparation and professional experience relevant to the programme they wish to pursue. The 2027–2028 call provides specialised training in areas connected to major development and professional challenges, including: Human rights Public health International and development economics Microfinance Food-chain safety Supply-chain management Cybersecurity Health-risk management Cultural conservation and collections management Disaster and risk management The programme therefore has potential relevance to professionals working in government, development organisations, NGOs, healthcare, finance, supply chains, technology, public administration, humanitarian work, research, education and other related fields. Programmes Available Under the ARES 2027–2028 Call Applicants should carefully examine the admission requirements of their preferred programme before beginning the application because academic and professional requirements can differ between programmes. 1. Specialised Bachelor s Degree The 2027–2028 call includes one specialised bachelor s programme: Specialised Bachelor s in Digital Integrated Supply Chain This programme is particularly relevant to candidates interested in modern supply-chain systems, logistics, digital transformation, procurement, international business and integrated supply-chain management. The programme may be particularly attractive to professionals whose careers involve logistics, procurement, supply-chain operations, business management, international development or related areas. The specialised bachelor s programme has a maximum duration of 12 months . 2. Eight Specialised Master s Programmes Applicants can also choose from eight specialised master s programmes covering a broad range of development-oriented disciplines. The available programmes include: Specialised Master s in Human Rights Specialised Master s in Integrated Health Risk Management Specialised Master in International and Development Economics Advanced Master in Microfinance Specialised Master s in Public Health Sciences – Analysis and Evaluation of International Health Policies, Programmes and Systems Specialised Master s in Food Chain Safety Management Specialised Master s in Preventive Conservation and Collections Management Specialised Master s in Risk and Disaster Management in the Anthropocene Era These programmes provide opportunities for professionals to deepen their expertise in fields that have significant relevance to sustainable development, public policy, health systems, economic development, food security, cultural heritage, disaster preparedness and humanitarian responses. The specialised master s programmes have a maximum duration of 12 months . 3. Continuing Education Programme The call also includes a continuing education opportunity: Certificate in Cybersecurity Operations and Risk Governance The programme focuses on cybersecurity operations and the governance of digital risks. It may be particularly relevant for professionals working in information technology, cybersecurity, digital governance, risk management and related fields. The continuing education programme has a maximum duration of six months . Who Can Apply for the ARES Scholarships? The ARES scholarships have specific eligibility requirements. Meeting one requirement alone does not necessarily make an applicant eligible. Candidates should satisfy the residency, employment, academic, professional experience and programme-specific admission requirements. 1. Applicants Must Be Connected to an Eligible Country Candidates must be permanent residents and workers in one of the 32 eligible countries . There is a specific exception for Palestinian nationals , who may qualify even when they do not reside in one of the 32 listed countries. This means that simply holding nationality from an eligible country may not be sufficient in every case. The call specifically refers to residence and employment requirements, so applicants should carefully review their circumstances before submitting an application. 2. Applicants Must Hold an Appropriate Higher Education Qualification Candidates must have an appropriate higher education qualification and satisfy the admission requirements of the programme they select. The relevant qualification must generally have been obtained no more than 20 years before the start of the programme . The maximum period can be extended by one additional year for each childbirth and/or adoption , according to the eligibility conditions provided in the call. Applicants should therefore examine the academic requirements of their selected programme rather than assuming that every university degree will automatically qualify them. 3. Professional Experience Is Required Applicants must demonstrate at least two years of relevant professional experience in one of the eligible countries. The experience must have been acquired after completion of the most recent graduate degree and before the application deadline . This requirement makes the scholarship particularly relevant to working professionals who already have experience in their field and want to acquire specialised international training that can strengthen their contribution to their organisations and communities. 4. Language Proficiency Applicants must complete their application in the language in which their chosen programme is taught . Candidates are expected to demonstrate good written and spoken command of the relevant teaching language. Applicants should therefore check the language requirements of their specific programme before applying. The scholarship information also notes that having a basic knowledge of French can be helpful for integration into everyday life in Belgium, even where the programme itself may have different language requirements. 5. Applicants Can Apply for Only One Programme One of the important rules of the ARES call is that an applicant may apply for only one programme . Applicants should therefore research the available courses carefully before submitting their application. Choosing a programme should involve considering: Academic background Professional experience Career objectives Programme admission requirements Language requirements Relevance to the applicant s professional field Long-term career plans Submitting applications for multiple programmes is not an appropriate strategy under this call. Which Countries Are Eligible? The ARES International Training Scholarships are open to applicants connected to 32 eligible partner countries across Africa, Asia, Southeast Asia, South America and the Caribbean. Eligible African Countries The African countries included in the call are: Benin Burkina Faso Burundi Cameroon Democratic Republic of the Congo Ethiopia Guinea Côte d’Ivoire Kenya Madagascar Mali Morocco Mozambique Niger Rwanda Senegal South Africa Tanzania Tunisia Uganda Zimbabwe Eligible Countries in South America and the Caribbean The eligible countries listed in this region are: Bolivia Cuba Ecuador Haiti Peru Eligible Southeast Asian Countries The eligible Southeast Asian countries are: Cambodia Indonesia Nepal Philippines Vietnam Eligible Asian Country Palestine Therefore, applicants from Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ethiopia, South Africa, Mozambique, Zimbabwe and the other listed partner countries can potentially apply, provided they satisfy all other eligibility requirements. Importantly, this is not a scholarship open to all African countries . Applicants should check the official country list before investing time in preparing an application. What Does the Scholarship Cover? The ARES International Training Scholarships provide substantial financial support to successful applicants. The support listed in the call includes several major categories. International Travel Expenses Scholarship recipients receive support for international travel expenses associated with their studies or training in Belgium. This can significantly reduce one of the major financial barriers faced by international applicants who need to travel to Europe for their programme. Subsistence Allowance The scholarship includes a subsistence allowance to help recipients meet living expenses during their period of study or training. This is particularly important for international students who may otherwise need to finance accommodation, food and other daily expenses independently. Tuition Fees For the specialised bachelor s and specialised master s programmes, the scholarship includes support for tuition fees . This means successful recipients can undertake their eligible programme without having to independently finance the applicable tuition costs covered by the scholarship. Visa-Related Expenses For specialised bachelor s and specialised master s recipients, the scholarship can cover exceptional costs associated with visa applications , subject to the conditions of the programme and scholarship. This provides additional financial support during the relocation process. Insurance Insurance costs are also included in the scholarship support. This provides an additional layer of financial protection for recipients while they are undertaking their programme in Belgium. Continuing Education Support For the continuing education programme, the financial package includes indirect mission expenses , alongside the applicable scholarship support described in the call. Because funding arrangements can differ depending on the programme type, applicants should consult the official call documentation for the exact financial conditions applicable to their selected programme. How Long Are the ARES Programmes? The duration depends on the type of programme selected. Specialised Bachelor s and Master s Programmes The specialised bachelor s and specialised master s programmes have a maximum duration of: 12 months Continuing Education The continuing education programme has a maximum duration of: 6 months Applicants should distinguish these programmes from conventional multi-year undergraduate or master s programmes. The ARES International Training call is focused on specialised training and academic programmes designed to strengthen the expertise of candidates who already possess relevant educational and professional backgrounds. How to Apply for the ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 Applications are submitted electronically through the ARES GIRAF platform . The application process involves several stages. Step 1: Create or Access Your GIRAF Account Applicants who already have a GIRAF account created and validated by ARES can log in using their existing account. Candidates who do not have a validated GIRAF account must complete the account creation request process. It is advisable to do this well before the deadline because applicants should not leave account creation and validation until the final hours of the application period. Step 2: Access the International Training Application After logging into GIRAF, navigate to: Competitive Calls Then select: Application – International Training 2027–2028 Applicants should click the application button only once, according to the application instructions. Step 3: Complete the Application Form Applicants should carefully complete all required sections of the form. Certain fields marked with an asterisk are mandatory and must be completed before the application can initially be saved. The system allows applicants to work on the application over multiple sessions. This means candidates do not necessarily need to complete everything in one sitting. Step 4: Save Your Application as a Draft If an applicant needs additional time to gather information or documents, the form can be saved as a draft. To continue a saved application, applicants should go to: Competitive Calls → My Tasks They can then select the relevant application and click: Open The applicant can continue editing the form as long as it remains a draft and has not been submitted. Step 5: Review the Application Carefully Before submission, applicants should check: Personal information Academic qualifications Employment history Professional experience Programme selection Language information Supporting documentation Eligibility information Contact details Any programme-specific requirements A careful final review is important because errors or missing information can affect the application. Step 6: Submit the Application Once everything has been completed and reviewed, the applicant can select: Submit my application After submission, the application will appear under: Competitive Calls → My Submitted Applications A crucial point is that an application cannot be modified after it has been submitted . Applicants should therefore avoid submitting prematurely. Important Application Deadline The deadline for the ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 is: Friday, 18 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Belgian time (UTC+1). Applications opened on 3 August 2026 . Applicants should not wait until the final day to create their GIRAF account, upload documents or submit the application. Because the deadline is based on Belgian time , international applicants should also account for the time difference between Belgium and their home country. Important Documents and Preparation Although exact documentation can depend on the selected programme, applicants should be prepared to provide evidence supporting their eligibility and application. Potentially relevant materials include: Academic certificates and diplomas Academic transcripts Evidence of professional experience Employment information Proof of residence Proof of nationality Language-related documentation where applicable Programme-specific documents Recommendation or reference information where required Any additional documentation requested by the selected programme Applicants should use the official ARES candidate guide and call documentation to determine exactly what must be submitted. It is also advisable to ensure that documents are clear, valid and prepared in the required language or format before beginning the final submission process. How to Strengthen Your ARES Scholarship Application Meeting the minimum requirements does not automatically guarantee selection. Applicants should therefore approach the application strategically. 1. Select a Programme That Matches Your Background Do not choose a programme simply because it is fully funded. Your academic background and professional experience should make sense in relation to your chosen field. For example, someone with professional experience in logistics, procurement, operations or supply-chain management may find the Digital Integrated Supply Chain programme particularly relevant. Similarly, someone working in public health should carefully examine the public-health and health-risk programmes. 2. Connect Your Professional Experience to Your Career Goals Your professional experience should demonstrate why the programme is useful for your career. Explain the skills you have already developed and identify the knowledge gaps that the programme will help you address. A strong application should create a logical connection between: Past experience → Current professional responsibilities → Selected programme → Future impact 3. Demonstrate Development Impact Because the programme is designed around international cooperation and capacity building, applicants should clearly demonstrate how advanced training could contribute to their institution, sector or wider community after completion. Think beyond personal advancement. Consider how the knowledge gained in Belgium could be applied to: Improve organisational systems Strengthen public services Develop innovative programmes Improve professional practices Address development challenges Build institutional capacity Transfer knowledge to colleagues Support sustainable development 4. Check Programme-Specific Admission Requirements One of the most important steps is to review the detailed admission requirements for the programme you intend to select. Different programmes can have different academic prerequisites and professional expectations. A candidate who meets the general ARES requirements may still fail to meet the admission conditions of a particular programme. 5. Start Early Do not treat the deadline as the date to begin the application. A better approach is to: Check eligibility. Research the programmes. Select one suitable programme. Create and validate your GIRAF account. Gather supporting documents. Complete the application. Review the information. Submit before the deadline. Starting early also gives you time to address technical or documentation problems. Why This Scholarship Is Valuable The ARES International Training Scholarships can provide more than financial assistance. For successful candidates, studying or undertaking professional training in Belgium can provide opportunities to: Gain specialised international academic training Develop advanced professional expertise Study in a European higher education environment Build international professional networks Learn from specialists and academic institutions Strengthen career prospects Acquire knowledge that can be applied in the home country Gain exposure to international approaches and practices Develop skills relevant to development challenges Expand professional and academic perspectives For mid-career professionals, the opportunity can be especially valuable because it combines international exposure with specialised training rather than simply providing a general academic qualification. Key Mistakes Applicants Should Avoid Applicants should be particularly careful to avoid the following mistakes: Applying for More Than One Programme The call permits applicants to apply for only one programme. Ignoring the Residency and Employment Requirement Being from an eligible country does not mean every applicant automatically qualifies. The residency and employment conditions should be carefully checked. Applying Without the Required Professional Experience The call requires at least two years of relevant professional experience under the stated conditions. Choosing a Programme Without Checking Academic Requirements Every programme can have specific admission requirements. Submitting an Incomplete Application Missing information or documentation can weaken an application or make it ineligible. Waiting Until the Deadline Technical issues, account validation, missing documents or last-minute errors can create serious problems. Forgetting That Submitted Applications Cannot Be Edited Applicants should review everything carefully before clicking the final submission button. Who Should Consider Applying? The opportunity may be particularly suitable for: Professionals from eligible developing and partner countries Graduates seeking advanced specialised training Mid-career professionals who want to strengthen their expertise Professionals working in development-related fields Public-sector employees NGO and civil-society professionals Health professionals Supply-chain and logistics professionals Economists and development practitioners Human-rights professionals Financial and microfinance specialists Food-safety professionals Disaster-risk and humanitarian practitioners Cybersecurity and technology professionals Professionals working in cultural heritage and collections management However, applicants should not rely solely on their professional field. They must also satisfy the official ARES eligibility requirements and the admission requirements of their selected programme. APPLY HERE Application Resources Applicants should consult the official ARES application information, candidate guidance and call documentation before submitting. The ARES candidate guide should be used to understand the GIRAF application process and submission requirements. Applicants should also consult the official 2027–2028 call reference document for the authoritative eligibility, programme and funding conditions. For questions concerning the scholarship call, the provided contact is: Maryvonne Aubry Email: scholarships-cooperation@ares-ac.be Visit HERE to learn more about the ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 in Belgium. Final Thoughts The ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 represent a significant opportunity for qualified professionals and graduates from 32 eligible partner countries to undertake specialised academic or professional training in Belgium with substantial financial support. The programme stands out because of the range of disciplines available. Applicants can pursue training connected to human rights, public health, international and development economics, microfinance, food-chain safety, cultural conservation, disaster and risk management, supply-chain management and cybersecurity. The scholarship is particularly suited to candidates who already have relevant academic qualifications and professional experience and who can clearly demonstrate how specialised international training will contribute to their professional development and wider impact. For eligible applicants, the most important next step is to verify the requirements of the specific programme they wish to pursue, prepare the required documentation and establish or validate their GIRAF account well before the deadline. Application deadline: 18 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Belgian time (UTC+1). Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and remember that once an application is submitted, it can no longer be modified . Always verify the latest requirements and instructions through the official ARES documentation before submitting. title: AKU Fall 2026 Virtual Internship Programme | Virtual Internships for Students
summary: The Aga Khan University (AKU) is inviting students to apply for its Fall 2026 Virtual Internship Programme (AKU-VIP) , an opportunity designed to help students gain practical professional experience, develop global perspectives, and build valuable career skills through fully virtual internships. The Fall 2026 cycle features a range of placements across the Aga Khan Development Network, including opportunities in education, school improvement, health sciences, communications, research, and partnerships . Students do not need to relocate or obtain a visa to participate. Through virtual project-based work, participants can collaborate with professionals in different countries while gaining experience that complements their academic studies and future career goals. About the AKU Virtual Internship Programme The Aga Khan University Virtual Internship Programme (AKU-VIP) provides students with structured virtual work placements with organizations within the Aga Khan Development Network. The programme is designed around the idea of gaining global experience while remaining locally based. Students can contribute to meaningful projects, interact with professional mentors, and develop an understanding of working in an international environment without the costs associated with international travel and relocation. Placements are available across 14 or more countries within the Aga Khan Development Network, giving participants exposure to organizations and professionals working across different regions and sectors. The programme combines flexibility with structured professional experience, making it suitable for students who want to develop their careers while continuing with their academic or personal commitments. Fall 2026 Internship Opportunities For the Fall 2026 cycle, students can apply for several virtual positions. Among the available placements are opportunities in education and school improvement. 1. Education Intern The Education Intern position is offered through the Centre for Innovation in Medical Education (CIME) at Aga Khan University in Nairobi, Kenya. This opportunity is particularly relevant to students interested in education, learning, innovation, research, and the development of effective educational approaches. The placement falls under the Health Sciences internship stream and provides students with an opportunity to gain professional experience while contributing to work connected to education and innovation. 2. School Improvement Programme Intern The School Improvement Programme Intern position is with Aga Khan Schools and is based with the Head Office in London, United Kingdom. This placement is particularly relevant to students interested in education, school improvement, teaching and learning, education systems, and programmes designed to strengthen school performance. The internship provides an opportunity to gain exposure to professional work focused on improving educational outcomes and supporting school development. Other Fall 2026 Virtual Internship Positions In addition to the education-focused opportunities, the Fall 2026 cycle includes other placements across different fields. Available positions listed for the cycle include: Communications Research Intern – Aga Khan Schools, Geneva, Switzerland Research Intern – Aga Khan University, Community Health Sciences, Karachi, Pakistan School Improvement Programme Intern – Aga Khan Schools, London, UK Partnerships and Research Intern – Aga Khan University, Centre of Excellence Women and Child Health, Nairobi, Kenya Education Intern – Aga Khan University, Centre for Innovation in Medical Education, Nairobi, Kenya Students should review the individual placement descriptions and Terms of Reference before applying because each position may have specific requirements, responsibilities, and application instructions. What Does the Virtual Internship Involve? AKU-VIP internships are designed around project-based professional work . Rather than simply observing an organization, interns contribute to projects and activities connected to their selected placement. The internships run for 12 weeks , with students expected to commit at least 15 hours per week . This structure gives students an opportunity to balance the internship with their academic and personal responsibilities while still gaining meaningful professional exposure. Depending on the placement, students may work on areas such as research, education, communications, project management, data analysis, healthcare, partnerships, and other professional activities. Why Apply for the AKU Virtual Internship Programme? Gain International Work Experience Students can gain experience working with organizations connected to an international development network without having to travel abroad. This can help participants understand professional practices in different countries and develop confidence working in multicultural environments. Develop Practical Career Skills The programme provides hands-on experience through project-based assignments. Students can develop skills that complement their academic qualifications and prepare them for future employment or further study. Build a Global Perspective Working virtually with professionals and organizations across different regions can expose participants to different approaches to problem-solving, education, development, research, and professional collaboration. Connect With Professionals The programme provides opportunities to interact with mentors and professionals working across the Aga Khan Development Network. These connections can help students expand their professional networks and gain insight into different career pathways. Flexible Virtual Format Because the programme is virtual, students can participate without relocating to the country where their host organization is located. The programme is designed to provide structure while maintaining flexibility around students academic and personal commitments. Strengthen Your CV Completing a structured international virtual internship can provide students with practical experience to include on their CVs, LinkedIn profiles, scholarship applications, graduate school applications, and future job applications. Programme Duration and Commitment Each AKU-VIP internship lasts for 12 weeks . Participants are expected to dedicate at least 15 hours per week to their internship activities. The virtual structure allows students to participate remotely while contributing to projects with their selected host institution. Applicants should therefore ensure that they can make the required time commitment before applying. How the Application Process Works The AKU Virtual Internship Programme follows a structured application process. Step 1: Online Application Students first submit an online application for their preferred internship placement. Applicants should carefully review the requirements and Terms of Reference for the position before submitting their application. Step 2: Virtual Interview Applicants who progress through the selection process may be invited to participate in a virtual interview. This gives the host organization an opportunity to assess the applicant s suitability for the placement. Step 3: Acceptance and Payment Successful applicants receive an acceptance and proceed with the required payment process. Applicants should review the programme s official fee information before applying so they understand the financial requirements associated with participation. Step 4: Internship Start Once the process is completed, accepted students begin their 12-week virtual internship with their selected host organization. Who Should Apply? The programme is suitable for students who want to gain practical experience and develop their professional skills while participating remotely. Students with interests in areas such as the following may find the available Fall 2026 placements particularly relevant: Education School improvement Research Health sciences Communications Partnerships Project management International development Professional and career development Applicants should also be prepared to work independently, communicate effectively online, meet deadlines, and dedicate the required hours each week to their internship. Because each placement has its own Terms of Reference, students should check the specific requirements of their preferred position before applying. Fall 2026 Deadline The application deadline for the Fall 2026 Virtual Internship Programme is: August 30, 2026 Students interested in participating should submit their applications before the deadline and allow sufficient time to review their preferred placement and prepare their application. How to Apply Interested students can learn more about the Aga Khan University Virtual Internship Programme and access the application through the official programme website. Application Website: www.aku.edu/vip Students can also review the available Fall 2026 placements and their individual Terms of Reference through the official Aga Khan University website before applying. Important Information for Applicants Before submitting an application, prospective applicants should: Review the available internship positions carefully. Identify a placement that matches their academic background and career interests. Read the Terms of Reference for their preferred position. Check the specific requirements and responsibilities of the placement. Confirm that they can commit at least 15 hours per week for 12 weeks. Prepare their application materials in advance. Take note of the programme s payment requirements. Submit their application before the August 30, 2026 deadline. Conclusion The Aga Khan University Fall 2026 Virtual Internship Programme offers students the opportunity to gain practical international experience without leaving their home country. With placements available across education, school improvement, research, health sciences, communications, and other fields, AKU-VIP can help students develop practical skills, expand their professional networks, gain global perspectives, and strengthen their career profiles. For students interested specifically in education, the Education Intern and School Improvement Programme Intern positions provide opportunities to contribute to work related to education and school development while gaining valuable professional experience. The Fall 2026 application deadline is August 30, 2026 . Discover more on the OFY Webpage . title: Team4Tech Experience AI Cohort 2026 | Free AI Education Training for NGOs in Africa
summary: Team4Tech is inviting education-focused nonprofits and NGOs operating in Africa to apply for its Experience AI Cohort , a free, structured learning programme designed to help nonprofit staff and teachers build practical knowledge and confidence in artificial intelligence and machine learning. Developed by the Raspberry Pi Foundation and Google DeepMind , Experience AI provides research-based educational resources for teachers and students aged 11–14 . Through the three-month cohort, selected organizations will participate in live virtual sessions, self-paced learning, coaching, and peer-learning activities to develop the skills needed to introduce AI literacy to their learning communities. About the Experience AI Cohort The programme will run from September through early December 2026 and will support participating NGOs in understanding the foundations of AI and implementing Experience AI lessons with teachers and learners. Participants will explore how AI is used in everyday life, how computers learn from data, and how issues such as limited datasets can contribute to bias. They will also gain practical experience training and testing machine learning models and learn strategies for identifying misinformation in an increasingly AI-driven world. The programme will also introduce participants to AI-related career pathways , helping educators prepare young people for a future where AI and digital skills are increasingly important. What Participants Will Learn Through the Experience AI programme, participants will: Explore how artificial intelligence is used in the world today. Understand how computers learn from data using machine learning. Discover how limited datasets can contribute to bias. Train and test a machine learning model to address a real-world problem. Develop strategies for distinguishing facts from false information in the age of AI. Learn about careers and opportunities related to artificial intelligence. Build confidence in delivering practical AI learning experiences. What Participating NGOs Will Receive Selected organizations will have access to: Research-based Experience AI resources and coursework. Live virtual learning and peer-learning sessions. Self-paced learning modules. Coaching and facilitation from Team4Tech. Opportunities to strengthen staff knowledge and practical AI skills. An implementation stipend upon successful completion of the required course activities. The stipend can be used to support the organization s implementation of the learning and strategies developed through the cohort. Who Can Apply? The opportunity is intended for education nonprofits and NGOs operating in Africa that are interested in using Experience AI lessons to strengthen AI literacy among teachers and learners. Participating organizations are expected to nominate 2–4 staff members who can commit approximately 15–20 total hours over three months . Organizations should also be prepared to: Complete asynchronous learning activities and assignments. Attend six live virtual sessions focused on peer learning, sharing, and feedback. Complete pre- and post-cohort surveys. Complete a follow-up survey approximately 4–6 months after participation. Develop plans for implementing Experience AI within their organization and learner community. Participants should also be comfortable completing coursework and participating in coaching sessions in English. Who Will Benefit? The programme is particularly relevant to organizations working with teachers and young learners aged 11–14 . By participating, NGOs can build their internal capacity to introduce young people to foundational AI concepts, responsible use of technology, machine learning, bias, misinformation, and AI-related careers. Organizations will also have the opportunity to share their learning with additional staff and teachers. Applicants are asked to indicate how many additional educators they expect to train on Experience AI lessons within the following 6–12 months . Expected Impact Experience AI can help participating organizations strengthen their education programmes by giving educators practical tools and knowledge to introduce AI concepts in an accessible way. Through the cohort, participating NGOs can develop strategies for integrating AI literacy into their existing programmes, help teachers become more confident in discussing AI with students, and give learners opportunities to understand how AI systems work rather than simply using AI tools. The programme can therefore contribute to stronger digital skills, AI awareness, critical thinking, and career readiness among young people. Important Dates Application Deadline: September 4, 2026 Selection Decisions: September 16–18, 2026 Programme Period: September 2026 – early December 2026 Up to 10 NGOs operating in Africa are expected to participate in the cohort. How to Apply Interested NGOs should complete the Experience AI Cohort application form before the September 4, 2026 deadline. Application: Apply for the Experience AI Cohort For questions specifically about the Experience AI cohort, applicants can contact Michelle Mwangi at michelle@team4tech.org . For other questions, contact community@team4tech.org . Conclusion The Team4Tech Experience AI Cohort 2026 provides African education nonprofits with an opportunity to strengthen their staff capacity in artificial intelligence and bring practical AI learning experiences to teachers and young people. With free coursework, live sessions, coaching, research-based resources, and an implementation stipend, the programme can help participating organizations take meaningful steps toward building AI-ready learning communities .
