title: Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program: Paid U.S. Internship Opportunity for Finance and Business Students
summary: The Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program offers an opportunity for ambitious university students to gain practical experience in financial services while developing their knowledge of credit, risk management, banking, and business operations. The internship is part of Truist s broad-based early-career internship programme, which combines education, professional exposure, and practical work experience. Through the Credit track, interns are connected with lines of business within Wholesale Banking , giving them an opportunity to develop an understanding of the day-to-day responsibilities involved in areas such as Commercial Corporate Banking, Specialized Industries and Wholesale Payments. The programme is designed for students who are interested in building careers in financial services and who want to complement their university education with hands-on experience in a major banking environment. The position was posted on August 18, 2026 , and is listed as available in five locations across the Truist footprint. The supplied job announcement does not specify a closing date, meaning interested candidates should not wait for a deadline before submitting an application. About the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program The Credit Internship Program is a temporary internship opportunity designed to develop early-career talent for roles connected to Truist s Wholesale Banking business. Rather than focusing exclusively on classroom learning, the programme combines structured training with practical assignments and exposure to real business activities. Interns can expect to participate in: Educational and professional development sessions. Business rotations. Special projects and assignments. Day-to-day business activities. Training related to credit and risk. Team-based projects. Activities involving internal business partners and external clients. Exposure to senior leaders and, potentially, executive leaders. This combination is intended to help interns understand how financial institutions operate while strengthening the technical, analytical, communication, and leadership capabilities required for a career in financial services. What Is the Credit Track? The Credit track is specifically aligned with business lines within Wholesale Banking . Interns may gain exposure to areas such as: Commercial and Corporate Banking This area involves supporting businesses and corporate clients with financial services and banking solutions. Interns can gain insight into how financial institutions evaluate business needs, manage relationships, and assess financial and credit considerations. Specialized Industries This area focuses on specific industry sectors and their unique financial requirements. Exposure to specialized industries can help interns understand how economic conditions, industry dynamics, and business models influence financial decision-making. Wholesale Payments Wholesale Payments focuses on financial solutions and payment services for business and institutional clients. Exposure to this area can help interns understand the role of financial infrastructure and payment systems in supporting businesses. The specific business area assigned to an intern will depend on the host team and programme placement. What Can Interns Expect During the Program? Truist describes the programme as one that combines education, exposure, and experience . This means successful interns are not simply expected to observe employees. They will have opportunities to participate in work that supports internal business partners and external clients while applying concepts learned during training. Interns will also be expected to work collaboratively and contribute to projects and activities assigned by their rotational leads. The programme is therefore suitable for students who want to gain practical experience while developing a deeper understanding of financial services. Exposure to Truist Senior Leaders One notable feature of the programme is exposure to Truist senior leadership. The internship may include sessions involving senior leaders and executive leaders, giving participants an opportunity to learn about the organization, its business operations, and the expectations associated with careers in financial services. For students preparing for careers in banking, finance, credit, or related areas, this type of professional exposure can provide useful insight into the financial-services industry and corporate leadership. Key Responsibilities of a Credit Intern Successful interns will be expected to undertake a range of responsibilities throughout the programme. 1. Learn Credit and Risk Management Concepts Interns will learn a broad range of concepts related to risk management, enterprise programmes and financial services. This training is intended to prepare them for assignments within different lines of business. 2. Develop Analytical and Decision-Making Skills Credit and financial-services careers require employees to evaluate information, identify risks, and make informed decisions. The programme therefore emphasizes the development of analytical and decision-making capabilities. Interns will have opportunities to apply these skills through practical projects and business assignments. 3. Strengthen Communication Skills Effective communication is an important requirement of the internship. Interns may work with internal business partners, external clients, managers, and other members of their teams. They will therefore need to communicate information clearly and professionally. 4. Develop Leadership Skills The programme also seeks to strengthen leadership capabilities. Students can develop leadership skills through project participation, teamwork, initiative, campus involvement, and other professional responsibilities. 5. Complete Special Projects Interns may be assigned special projects or other tasks outside the formal training programme. These assignments can provide opportunities to demonstrate initiative, analytical thinking, organization and problem-solving skills. 6. Participate in Business Rotations Business rotations form an important part of the programme. Through rotations, interns can work on projects and participate in normal business activities, allowing them to apply concepts and behaviours learned during training. 7. Complete Additional Training Managers may recommend additional training during or after the internship programme. This can help interns continue developing relevant skills and knowledge based on their assignments and career interests. Academic Requirements The Truist Credit Internship Program is intended for students who are actively pursuing a university degree. Applicants must be working toward either: A Bachelor’s degree; or A Master’s degree. Truist particularly values candidates studying business-related disciplines , with accounting and finance coursework preferred. A 3.0 or higher GPA is preferred . The GPA requirement is described as preferred rather than an absolute minimum, meaning candidates should carefully review the complete application requirements rather than assuming that applicants below 3.0 are automatically excluded. Graduation Requirement Another important requirement concerns the expected graduation date. Applicants should have a scheduled final-degree graduation date between the following: December 2027 and June 2029. Students outside this graduation window may therefore not fit the target profile for this particular internship programme. Prospective applicants should carefully compare their expected graduation date with the requirement before applying. Skills Truist Is Looking For The programme is designed for students who can demonstrate a combination of academic preparation, interpersonal abilities, and professional potential. Important skills and qualities include: Strong Communication Candidates should possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills. This is important because interns may work with multiple stakeholders, participate in meetings, collaborate on projects, and potentially interact with clients. Initiative Truist seeks students who demonstrate strong initiative. Applicants should be able to show situations where they have taken responsibility, identified opportunities, solved problems, or gone beyond basic expectations. Leadership Demonstrated leadership is another important requirement. Leadership may be demonstrated through: Campus organizations. Student leadership positions. Volunteer activities. Work experience. Academic projects. Community initiatives. Team activities. Other situations where the applicant has taken responsibility and influenced positive outcomes. Analytical Ability Because the Credit track is associated with credit and risk, analytical thinking is highly relevant. Students should be comfortable working with information, evaluating situations, and drawing logical conclusions. Financial Services Interest Candidates should have genuine enthusiasm for pursuing a career in financial services. A demonstrated interest in banking, finance, credit, accounting, risk management, or related fields can strengthen an applicant s profile. Technical Skills Required Applicants should be proficient in: Microsoft Excel Microsoft PowerPoint Excel is particularly useful in financial-services environments where employees may work with financial information, calculations, analysis, and reporting. PowerPoint can be useful for presentations, project updates, business proposals, and communicating analytical findings. Students should therefore ensure that they can confidently use both programmes before entering the internship. Financial Services Knowledge Truist also seeks candidates with general knowledge of the financial services industry. Students should therefore understand fundamental concepts related to banking, finance, credit, and risk. Applicants do not necessarily need extensive professional experience because the programme is designed for early-career talent. title: University of Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship 2027: Fully Funded Undergraduate Opportunity for International Students
summary: The University of Toronto Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship 2027 presents an exceptional opportunity for outstanding international students seeking to pursue an undergraduate degree in Canada. Recognized as the University of Toronto s most prestigious scholarship for international students, the programme is designed to support exceptional young people who demonstrate outstanding academic achievement, creativity, leadership potential, and the ability to make a positive contribution to the global community. The highly competitive scholarship provides comprehensive financial support for four years of undergraduate study at the University of Toronto , covering tuition, books, incidental fees, and full residence support. Approximately 37 students are selected as Pearson Scholars each year , making this one of the most significant undergraduate scholarship opportunities available to international students in Canada. For prospective students looking for a fully funded undergraduate scholarship in Canada, the Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship offers not only financial assistance but also the opportunity to join a diverse international community at one of Canada s leading universities. What Is the Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship? The Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship is a prestigious University of Toronto scholarship created to recognize exceptional international students entering first-entry undergraduate programmes. The scholarship focuses on students who have demonstrated more than academic excellence. The University of Toronto seeks candidates who have shown creativity, leadership potential, and a commitment to contributing positively to the global community . Pearson Scholars become part of a global community of exceptional students and gain access to the University of Toronto s academic environment, resources, and broader international student community. The scholarship is particularly significant because it provides financial support for the full duration of an undergraduate programme, helping successful students overcome some of the major financial barriers associated with studying in Canada. What Does the Pearson Scholarship Cover? One of the most attractive features of the Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is its comprehensive financial coverage. Successful scholars receive support covering: Tuition fees for four years. Books required during their studies. Incidental fees associated with their university education. Full residence support for four years. The scholarship is tenable only at the University of Toronto and applies to first-entry undergraduate programmes . This means applicants should understand that the scholarship is specifically designed for students entering undergraduate studies rather than students who are already enrolled in post-secondary education. The University of Toronto describes the programme as one of the largest scholarship programmes for international students in Canada. The programme has previously attracted students from around the world, with the university reporting representation from 188 countries . How Competitive Is the University of Toronto Pearson Scholarship? The Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is highly competitive. Approximately 37 students are named Pearson Scholars each year , meaning applicants are selected from a very strong international pool of candidates. The university s selection criteria go beyond academic grades. Applicants are expected to demonstrate a combination of: Outstanding academic achievement. Creativity. Leadership potential. A demonstrated ability or potential to contribute positively to the global community. Students therefore should not approach the scholarship application as simply an academic award. Their wider achievements, leadership experiences, creativity, personal qualities and potential impact are important components of the opportunity. Who Is Eligible for the Pearson International Scholarship 2027? To be considered for the Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship 2027, applicants must satisfy the University of Toronto s eligibility requirements. Applicants must be international students , meaning they must be non-Canadian students who require a study permit to study in Canada. They must also meet the relevant secondary-school requirements. For the 2027 scholarship, eligible students must be: Enrolled in their final year of senior secondary school during the 2026–2027 academic year ; or Have graduated from secondary school no earlier than June 2026 . In addition, successful candidates must be prepared to begin their undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto in September 2027 . Who Is Not Eligible? The University of Toronto also identifies circumstances in which students cannot be considered for the Pearson Scholarship. Students are not eligible if they are already attending post-secondary studies. Students who begin their post-secondary studies in January 2027 , whether at the University of Toronto or another post-secondary institution, are also not eligible. The scholarship is therefore specifically targeted at students transitioning from secondary school into their first-entry undergraduate programme at the University of Toronto. High School Nomination Is Mandatory An important feature of the Lester B. Pearson Scholarship is that students cannot simply apply independently without a school nomination . Applicants must first be nominated by their current secondary school. Students should therefore speak with their Guidance counsellor; Principal; Head of school; or Another appropriate school official responsible for scholarship nominations. Each eligible high school can nominate only one student per year . This makes it important for prospective applicants to begin discussions with their schools well before the nomination deadline. Students should explain their academic achievements, leadership experiences, extracurricular activities, community involvement, and other accomplishments to their school so that the school can make an informed decision about its nominee. What If Your School Has Never Participated? The University of Toronto allows schools that have not previously participated in the Pearson Scholarship programme to apply to join the programme. Schools that have previously participated will receive access to the nomination form beginning July 6, 2026 . The deadline for schools to nominate a student is October 9, 2026. Schools that have not previously participated can apply to join the programme by noon Eastern Standard Time on October 9, 2026 . Students whose schools have not participated previously should therefore raise the opportunity with their school administration as early as possible. University of Toronto Admission Application Being nominated by a secondary school is only one part of the Pearson Scholarship process. After nomination, the student must also apply for admission to the University of Toronto. To be considered for the scholarship, applicants must apply to at least one undergraduate programme at the University of Toronto and plan to begin their studies in September 2027. The deadline to apply for admission to the University of Toronto and be considered for the Pearson Scholarship is: October 16, 2026. Applicants can apply to up to three areas of study on their University of Toronto admission application. However, applicants should pay close attention to the university s rules because, if they receive the Pearson Scholarship, the award will be restricted to their top choice of programme at the time scholarship decisions are made . Pearson Scholarship Application Deadline After being nominated by their school and submitting their University of Toronto admission application, eligible nominees will receive a private link to the Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship application. The scholarship application can be completed only after the student has submitted their University of Toronto admission application. The final deadline to complete the Pearson Scholarship application and submit all required documentation is November 6, 2026. Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final day. Because the process involves school nomination, university admission, and a separate scholarship application, prospective candidates should plan their applications several weeks or months in advance. Key Pearson Scholarship 2027 Deadlines The major dates prospective applicants should remember are: July 6, 2026 – Participating high schools receive access to the nomination form. October 9, 2026 – Deadline for high school nominations. October 9, 2026, by noon EST – Deadline for schools that have never participated to apply to join the programme. October 16, 2026 – Deadline for students to submit their University of Toronto admission application and be considered for the scholarship. November 6, 2026 – Final deadline for completing the Pearson Scholarship application and submitting the required documentation. September 2027 – Successful scholars begin their undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto. What Makes a Strong Pearson Scholarship Candidate? Because the scholarship is highly competitive, applicants should understand that simply meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee selection. The University of Toronto specifically identifies three major qualities among Pearson Scholars: 1. Academic Excellence Applicants should have a strong academic record and demonstrate exceptional achievement during their secondary education. Academic performance provides an important foundation for the scholarship because Pearson Scholars are expected to succeed in a demanding university environment. 2. Creativity The scholarship also recognizes creativity. This does not necessarily mean creativity only in artistic activities. Students can demonstrate creativity through innovation, problem-solving, entrepreneurship, research, technology, community projects, leadership initiatives or other activities where they have developed original approaches to challenges. 3. Leadership Potential Leadership is another important consideration. Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate situations in which they have taken initiative, influenced others, organized activities, solved problems, supported their communities or contributed meaningfully to their schools or wider society. Leadership does not necessarily require holding a formal title. What matters is the impact and initiative demonstrated by the applicant. Why International Students Should Consider This Opportunity For international students seeking an undergraduate scholarship in Canada, the Pearson Scholarship stands out because of its extensive financial coverage. Studying internationally can involve substantial costs, including tuition, accommodation, books and other university-related expenses. The Pearson Scholarship addresses several of these costs through its four-year financial support package. Beyond financial assistance, the scholarship offers successful students the opportunity to study at the University of Toronto and become part of an internationally diverse academic community. The programme s global reach is also reflected in the university s reported representation of scholars from 188 countries . The Importance of Starting Early One of the most important considerations for students interested in the Lester B. Pearson Scholarship is the multi-stage application process. Unlike scholarships where students submit a single independent application, Pearson requires applicants to coordinate several stages. A prospective applicant should begin by determining whether their secondary school can nominate a student. The applicant should then discuss the opportunity with the appropriate school official, prepare for the University of Toronto admission process, identify suitable undergraduate programmes and ensure that all application requirements are completed before the relevant deadlines. Starting early can also give students more time to prepare information about their academic achievements, leadership activities, creative projects, community involvement and future aspirations. Recommended Application Preparation Strategy Students interested in applying for the Pearson Scholarship can take a structured approach. Step 1: Confirm Your Eligibility First, determine whether you meet the international student, secondary-school and university-entry requirements. Make sure you will be starting your undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto in September 2027. Step 2: Speak to Your School Contact your guidance counsellor, principal or head of school. Ask whether the school is eligible to nominate a student for the Lester B. Pearson Scholarship. If the school has not participated previously, encourage the relevant school official to review the requirements for joining the programme. Step 3: Build Your Academic Profile Review your academic record and identify your strongest achievements. Keep evidence of major academic awards, competitions, research activities, projects and other accomplishments that demonstrate excellence. Step 4: Document Your Leadership and Community Activities Prepare a clear record of leadership positions, volunteer activities, school initiatives, community projects, extracurricular activities and other contributions. Rather than simply listing activities, applicants should understand the impact they made through those experiences. Step 5: Prepare Your University Application Research the University of Toronto s undergraduate programmes and determine which programmes align with your academic interests and career goals. Remember that applicants can apply to up to three areas on their admission application, while the scholarship, if awarded, will be associated with the applicant s top programme choice at the relevant decision stage. Step 6: Submit the Admission Application The University of Toronto admission application must be submitted by the relevant deadline of October 16, 2026 for students seeking consideration for the Pearson Scholarship. Step 7: Complete the Pearson Scholarship Application After school nomination and submission of the university admission application, the nominee will receive a private link to the Pearson Scholarship application. Complete the application carefully and submit all required documentation by November 6, 2026 . Important Fraud Warning for Applicants Prospective Pearson Scholars should be extremely cautious about individuals or organizations claiming that they can secure a scholarship, guarantee acceptance, or provide an official University of Toronto scholarship nomination in exchange for money. The University of Toronto has specifically warned applicants about fraudulent emails and organizations claiming to assist students with Lester B. Pearson Scholarship applications. The university states that the Lester B. Pearson Scholarship programme does not work with agencies or educational agents to recruit students or offer scholarships . Applicants should therefore be cautious if someone Promises guaranteed scholarship selection; Offers a scholarship acceptance for a fee; Claims to be an official Pearson Scholarship agent; Requests money to secure a nomination; Provides suspicious acceptance letters; or Requests payment to submit an application on the student s behalf. Pearson Scholarship recipients can only be nominated by their current secondary school through the university s official online process . Students should rely on official University of Toronto information and avoid paying unaffiliated third parties for scholarship assistance. What Happens After Selection? Successful students become Pearson Scholars and join a global community of exceptional students at the University of Toronto. The Pearson Program Office, housed within the University s Centre for International Experience, provides enrichment and support opportunities for Pearson Scholars during their studies. This can provide scholars with opportunities to engage beyond their academic programmes and participate in activities designed to enrich their international university experience. Financial Support at a Glance The Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship provides the following: Four years of undergraduate scholarship support. Tuition coverage. Book support. Coverage of incidental fees. Full residence support. Study at the University of Toronto. Membership in an international community of Pearson Scholars. Nationality and Country Eligibility An important point for prospective international applicants is that eligibility is not simply determined by nationality . The official eligibility guidance explains that this can include British or Irish nationals, individuals with Indefinite Leave to Remain or Right of Abode, and individuals with settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, subject to the relevant residence requirements. There are also other routes to Home Fee status depending on citizenship, immigration/residency status and family circumstances. Refugees and people with humanitarian protection in the UK may also qualify in relevant circumstances. Applicants should therefore not assume that holding a particular nationality automatically makes them eligible or ineligible . The decisive issue is whether they meet the programme s Home Fee status and other eligibility requirements. The Foundation s eligibility guidance should be checked carefully before applying. UK and Ireland Schooling Requirement The 2027 eligibility requirements also include an educational history condition. Applicants generally need to have attended school in the UK or Ireland for at least three years between the ages of 11 and 18 , or for at least seven years between the ages of 4 and 18. The periods do not necessarily need to be continuous. There are specific provisions for refugees, stateless people and asylum seekers, so applicants in these circumstances should review the detailed eligibility guidance rather than relying solely on the general rule. When Does the Application Open? Applications for the 2027 Martingale Scholarships opened on: 12 August 2026 The Foundation encourages applicants to begin preparing early and to read the application guidance carefully before submitting their forms. Martingale Scholarship 2027 Deadline The final application deadline is: 18 October 2026 at 23:59 UK time. Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications. Martingale recommends allowing sufficient time to complete the application and ensure that all required information is submitted correctly. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, although the final shortlisting decision is made after the application deadline. 2027 Martingale Scholarship Application Timeline The programme follows several stages: Stage 1: Apply to Martingale Applicants complete the Martingale online application form. The application asks candidates about areas including: Educational background Academic qualifications Family background Financial circumstances Motivation for postgraduate research Academic interests Personal circumstances Applicants also need to provide an academic transcript, evidence of financial need and two referees. Stage 2: Interview Shortlisted applicants are invited to an in-person interview. The interviews are scheduled for November 2026 and are expected to take place across the UK. The interview assesses areas including: Academic interests Technical ability Academic potential Motivation for postgraduate study and research Potential contribution to the Martingale Scholar cohort Stage 3: Become a Martingale Qualified Candidate Candidates who successfully progress through the selection process may become Martingale Qualified Candidates . This is an important stage, but becoming a Qualified Candidate does not automatically guarantee a scholarship. Qualified Candidates receive support when applying to eligible programmes at partner universities. Stage 4: Apply to Partner Universities Qualified Candidates then apply directly to one or more partner universities for eligible Master s or PhD courses. Each university has its own admissions process and deadline, meaning applicants must carefully monitor the requirements of every university and programme they apply to. Martingale provides application support during this stage. Stage 5: University Offers and Funding Allocation For Master s candidates, successful applicants who receive offers from eligible courses submit their university and course preferences to Martingale, which then allocates funded places among successful candidates. For PhD candidates, partner universities make offers of Martingale PhD places directly to Qualified Candidates, subject to available places and university decisions. A university offer may be conditional, in which case the associated Martingale funding is also conditional. Key Dates for the 2027 Scholarship The published timeline includes: 12 August 2026: Applications open. 18 October 2026: Final application deadline at 23:59. November 2026: Interviews. December 2026: Applicants are notified of outcomes. December 2026: PhD Showcase. December 2026–January 2027: Martingale application support. January–February 2027: Applications to partner universities. March 2027: Confirmation of university offers. April 2027: Offers of Martingale-funded places. Some university programmes may have earlier admissions deadlines, so candidates must check the individual requirements of each programme. Important: Becoming a Qualified Candidate Does Not Guarantee Funding Applicants should understand the distinction between becoming a Martingale Qualified Candidate and receiving a Martingale Scholarship . Qualified Candidate status means that an applicant has successfully passed the Martingale selection stage and is eligible to be considered for funding for eligible courses. However, the number of Qualified Candidates can be greater than the number of available scholarship places. A candidate may therefore become Qualified but not immediately receive a scholarship. Some Qualified Candidates may be placed on a waitlist, while others may receive funding later if additional places become available. Martingale strongly encourages Qualified Candidates to apply to multiple partner universities to increase their chances of being matched with a funded place. How to Prepare a Strong Application Prospective applicants can take several steps to strengthen their applications. 1. Confirm Your Eligibility Before spending significant time on the application, carefully review the official eligibility criteria, particularly the requirements concerning: Academic achievement Home Fee status UK or Ireland schooling history School funding background Financial circumstances Eligible postgraduate study Relevant academic subject 2. Research the Available Courses Do not apply based only on the reputation of a university. Study the actual 2027 Martingale-funded courses and check: Course content Entry requirements Academic prerequisites Research areas University application deadlines Whether the programme is suitable for your career and research ambitions 3. Explain Your Research Motivation Clearly The programme is specifically focused on postgraduate research. Applicants should therefore be prepared to explain why they want to pursue advanced study, what academic areas interest them and how postgraduate research fits into their longer-term goals. 4. Prepare Financial Information Carefully Because financial need is an important component of the programme, applicants should ensure that their financial information is accurate and complete. Martingale uses multiple indicators to assess socioeconomic circumstances, rather than relying exclusively on household income. 5. Start Early Although applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and final shortlisting takes place after the deadline, applicants are encouraged to begin and submit their applications as soon as they are ready. Starting early gives applicants more time to: Gather academic records Contact referees Prepare financial information Review their personal statements Research eligible courses Check university requirements Correct errors before submission Why the Martingale Scholarship Is More Than Tuition Funding A major strength of the programme is that it combines financial support with long-term development. A traditional scholarship may primarily address tuition or living costs. Martingale s model also seeks to develop the scholar s academic, leadership, communication and professional capabilities. For Master s scholars, the Development Programme provides opportunities to build confidence, communication and networking skills while engaging with academics and industry. For PhD scholars, the Leadership Programme continues this development over multiple years, helping participants build the skills needed to navigate careers in research, academia, industry and other sectors. Official Application and Further Information Applicants should use the Martingale Foundation s official resources for the most current information, including eligibility guidance, application instructions, courses and participating universities. Apply here Learn more here Conclusion The 2027 Martingale Scholarships provide a comprehensive route into postgraduate research for talented students who may face financial and socioeconomic barriers to advanced study. The programme combines funding for tuition, research expenses and living costs with university application support, professional development, leadership training and access to a growing community of researchers and professionals. For the 2027 intake, the opportunity is focused on eligible Master s and PhD programmes in mathematical sciences and artificial intelligence at participating UK research universities. Prospective applicants should carefully check their eligibility, investigate the available courses, prepare their academic and financial information and begin their applications well before the 18 October 2026 at 23:59 deadline . Because eligibility involves more than nationality alone, applicants should pay particular attention to the requirements surrounding Home Fee status, UK or Ireland schooling history, academic attainment and socioeconomic circumstances . Checking the official eligibility guidance is essential before submitting an application. For eligible students with the ambition to pursue advanced research in mathematics or artificial intelligence, the Martingale Scholarship represents not only financial assistance for postgraduate study, but also an opportunity to join a structured community designed to help emerging researchers develop academically, professionally and as future leaders. title: ETH Zurich PhD Student in Macroeconomic Forecasting and Data Science: Apply by 15 September 2026
summary: ETH Zurich is inviting qualified candidates to apply for a PhD Student position in Macroeconomic Forecasting and Data Science at the KOF Swiss Economic Institute in Zurich, Switzerland. The full-time position offers an opportunity for a highly motivated graduate with a strong background in economics, econometrics, data science, statistics or another closely related quantitative discipline to pursue doctoral research while contributing to internationally relevant economic forecasting activities. The position is offered at 100% employment on a fixed-term basis and is available immediately, with ETH Zurich indicating that the successful candidate should ideally be able to take up the position as soon as possible. The application deadline is 15 September 2026 . About the ETH Zurich PhD Position The position is based at the KOF Swiss Economic Institute at ETH Zurich , one of Switzerland s leading centres for applied economic research. The successful candidate will join the Research Division for Macroeconomic Forecasting and Data Science , a research environment that combines traditional macroeconomic analysis with modern data science and computational approaches. The division focuses on analysing and forecasting both the Swiss and international economies. Its work contributes to KOF s short- and medium-term economic outlooks through the use of macroeconometric models, economic indicators, survey information, and increasingly sophisticated data science techniques. The research environment brings together several important areas, including: Macroeconomic modelling Macroeconometrics Economic forecasting Economic nowcasting Time-series econometrics Machine learning High-frequency economic indicators Large-scale economic datasets Forecasting evaluation Data pipelines and research software This makes the position particularly relevant for graduates who want to develop advanced expertise at the intersection of economics, econometrics, data science, and policy-oriented research . Key Responsibilities The successful PhD student will undertake doctoral research while participating in the activities of the Macroeconomic Forecasting and Data Science research division. 1. Contribute to international economic forecasting One of the core responsibilities will be participation in the preparation of the international economic outlook as part of KOF s quarterly economic forecasting publications. This will provide the successful candidate with an opportunity to work on real-world economic analysis and contribute to research that informs understanding of international economic developments. 2. Pursue a high-quality Ph.D. The position is designed around the completion of an excellent doctoral dissertation in an area such as: Applied macroeconomics Macroeconometrics Economic nowcasting Economic forecasting The PhD component means that the successful candidate will be expected to undertake rigorous academic research while developing work capable of making a meaningful contribution to the field. 3. Develop forecasting and nowcasting models The candidate will be involved in developing, implementing, and evaluating new models for economic forecasting and nowcasting. This work may involve combining established econometric approaches with modern machine-learning techniques to improve the ability to analyse economic developments and generate forecasts. 4. Work with large-scale economic datasets The position involves analysing large-scale and high-frequency datasets with the objective of improving economic forecasting. Applicants interested in working with complex, real-time, and high-volume economic data will therefore find the position particularly relevant. 5. Develop reproducible research systems The successful candidate will also be expected to develop and maintain: Reproducible code Data pipelines Research software Analytical workflows This requirement highlights the importance of strong programming and data-management skills alongside traditional economic research capabilities. Required Academic Background Applicants should have an excellent academic record and must hold, or be expected to have completed by the time of appointment, a Master s degree in one of the following areas: Economics Econometrics Data Science Statistics A closely related quantitative discipline The position is therefore particularly suited to candidates whose postgraduate education has given them a strong foundation in quantitative analysis and research. Academic excellence is an important part of the selection criteria, as the successful candidate will be expected to undertake demanding doctoral research while contributing to KOF s applied economic research activities. Technical and Research Skills Candidates should demonstrate strong quantitative and programming capabilities. A strong understanding of time-series econometrics and forecasting methods is highly relevant. Applicants who do not possess all of these skills but have a strong interest and demonstrated capacity to acquire them may also be considered, according to the stated profile. Experience or a strong interest in the following areas will be valuable: Large-scale datasets Real-time economic data Nowcasting Forecasting Forecasting evaluation Time-series analysis Econometric modelling Machine learning Economic data analysis Research programming The role therefore combines academic economics with practical computational and data-science applications. Communication and Language Requirements Communication skills are another important component of the position. Candidates are expected to have excellent Verbal communication skills Written communication skills Visual communication skills Academic and research writing abilities The position specifically requires applicants to be comfortable writing in German and English . Importantly, good command of German is a prerequisite for the position. Applicants should therefore carefully assess their German-language proficiency before applying. Knowledge of French or Italian is considered an additional asset but is not listed as a mandatory requirement. Employment Terms and PhD Duration The position is offered at 100% employment in Zurich and is initially fixed-term. ETH Zurich states that the appointment will initially be for 18 months , with the prospect of extension for the normal four- to five-year duration of the doctorate , subject to satisfactory progress. The starting date is negotiable, although the position is available immediately and the institution would like it to be filled as soon as possible. The gross salary will be determined in accordance with the applicable ETH Zurich salary regulations . What ETH Zurich Offers The position provides an opportunity to pursue doctoral research at a globally recognised scientific and technological university while working within a dynamic and collaborative research environment. ETH Zurich states that it offers internationally competitive employment conditions and support for professional development. The broader employment environment includes opportunities such as Professional and personal development support Training and further education opportunities A flexible working environment A supportive learning environment Health-related service discounts Sports activities through the university s sports association Childcare support These provisions are designed to support employees not only in their academic and professional development but also in maintaining a supportive working environment. Research Environment at KOF Swiss Economic Institute The KOF Swiss Economic Institute is the research institution within ETH Zurich where the successful candidate will be based. Its Macroeconomic Forecasting and Data Science division brings together economic research and computational techniques to understand economic developments and produce forecasts. The division s work is particularly relevant in an environment where economic conditions can change rapidly and where policymakers, businesses, and researchers increasingly rely on timely economic information. By combining macroeconometric models, economic indicators, survey information, high-frequency data, and machine learning techniques, the research environment provides an opportunity for doctoral researchers to work on contemporary challenges in economic forecasting. Diversity and Sustainability at ETH Zurich ETH Zurich states that it is committed to an inclusive culture based on equality of opportunity, diversity, and respect for the rights and dignity of staff and students. The institution promotes a working and learning environment in which individuals can develop and contribute regardless of their background. Sustainability is also identified as a core institutional value, with ETH Zurich working toward a climate-neutral future. These institutional commitments form part of the broader environment in which the successful PhD student will undertake their studies and research. Application Requirements Applicants must submit their applications online through the designated ETH Zurich application portal. The application must include the following documents: Letter of motivation explaining why the applicant is interested in pursuing a PhD in economic forecasting. Curriculum vitae (CV) outlining academic qualifications, research experience, professional experience, and relevant skills. Writing samples in German or English , such as a Master s thesis. Complete academic record , including undergraduate and graduate courses and grades. Copies of academic certificates . Contact information for two to three potential referees . Applicants should ensure that their documents clearly demonstrate their academic preparation, quantitative abilities, research interests, and suitability for doctoral work in macroeconomic forecasting and data science. Application Deadline The deadline for submitting applications is: 15 September 2026 Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day. The institution also states that the position is available immediately and should be filled as soon as possible , while the starting date itself remains negotiable. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the official online application portal. ETH Zurich specifically states that it only accepts applications submitted through its online application portal . Applications sent by email or postal services will not be considered. Applicants should therefore prepare all required documents in advance and submit the complete application through the designated recruitment system. Questions concerning the position or application procedure can be directed to the KOF HR Services team at hr@kof.ethz.ch . The email address is intended for questions and not for submitting applications. APPLY HERE Why This PhD Opportunity Stands Out This position stands out because it combines a formal doctoral programme with direct involvement in applied economic research. Rather than focusing exclusively on theoretical academic work, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to contribute to economic forecasting activities while developing a PhD in applied macroeconomics, macroeconometrics, or economic nowcasting or forecasting. The position is especially relevant to candidates interested in the growing intersection between the following: Economics and data science Macroeconomics and machine learning Econometrics and artificial intelligence Economic forecasting and real-time data Academic research and policy analysis Quantitative research and programming The opportunity can therefore provide a strong research platform for someone seeking advanced expertise in modern economic forecasting. About ETH Zurich ETH Zurich is a leading university specialising in science and technology and is internationally recognised for education, fundamental research, and the transfer of knowledge into society. The university has a large international community, with more than 30,000 people from more than 120 countries. Its location in the heart of Europe also provides an international academic and research environment. For candidates interested in pursuing a career in academic research, economic analysis, data science, or evidence-based policy research, undertaking a PhD at an institution of this standing can provide exposure to a highly research-intensive environment. Important Points for Prospective Applicants Before applying, candidates should pay particular attention to the following requirements: The position is full-time at 100% . The position is based in Zurich, Switzerland . It is initially offered for 18 months . There is potential for extension to the normal four- to five-year doctoral period , subject to satisfactory progress. A relevant Master s degree is required or must be completed by appointment. Strong quantitative and programming abilities are important. Knowledge or interest in time-series econometrics, forecasting, and nowcasting is highly relevant. Experience with large-scale or real-time datasets is valuable. Good German is a prerequisite . English and German writing skills are required. French or Italian is an added advantage. Applicants must provide a writing sample. Complete academic records and certificates are required. Applicants must provide contact details for two to three references . Applications must be submitted online. Email and postal applications will not be considered. The application deadline is 15 September 2026 . The position is available immediately and is intended to be filled as soon as possible. Visit HERE for more information about the ETH Zurich PhD Student in Macroeconomic Forecasting and Data Science. Conclusion The ETH Zurich PhD Student in Macroeconomic Forecasting and Data Science position presents an opportunity for a highly qualified quantitative researcher to combine doctoral studies with practical, policy-relevant economic research at the KOF Swiss Economic Institute. With its focus on applied macroeconomics, macroeconometrics, economic nowcasting, forecasting, machine learning, high-frequency data, and reproducible research, the position is particularly suited to graduates who want to build advanced expertise at the intersection of economics and data science. Candidates with a relevant Master s degree, excellent academic performance, strong quantitative and programming capabilities, an interest in economic forecasting, and the required German and English communication skills should consider preparing their applications carefully. Interested applicants should ensure that their motivation letter, CV, academic records, writing sample, certificates, and references are complete before submitting their application through the official online portal. title: NICEF Partnerships Officer, NO-1, Fixed-Term Job in Pretoria, South Africa: Apply by August 28, 2026
summary: If you are a development, international relations, communications, public policy, or partnerships professional looking for an opportunity with the United Nations system, UNICEF is inviting applications for a Partnerships Officer, NO-1, Fixed-Term Appointment in Pretoria, South Africa . The successful candidate will work within the UNICEF South Africa Country Office and contribute to efforts aimed at strengthening investments and opportunities for children.
